structures.label: Stomach
structures.summary: The stomach is a muscular, expandable organ located between the esophagus and the duodenum.

structures.label: Liver
structures.summary: The liver is one of the body's largest and most metabolically active organs. Its functions extend well beyond digestion.

structures.label: Gallbladder
structures.summary: The gallbladder stores and concentrates bile produced by the liver.

structures.label: Pancreas
structures.summary: The pancreas is an accessory digestive organ with both exocrine and endocrine functions.

structures.label: Duodenum
structures.summary: The first and shortest region, approximately 25 cm long. It receives acidic chyme from the stomach along with bile and pancreatic secretions.

structures.label: Small intestine
structures.summary: The small intestine is the primary site of chemical digestion and nutrient absorption.

structures.label: Large intestine
structures.summary: The large intestine is the final major region of the digestive tract. It consists of the cecum, colon, rectum, and anal canal.

structures.label: Esophagus
structures.summary: The esophagus transports food primarily through muscular contractions rather than gravity, allowing swallowing even when the body is horizontal or inverted.
